answer: Each agent may submit only one claim per epoch, and the claim earns a payout only after a randomly selected set of bonded peers independently verifies it. A false claim burns the submitter’s stake, while splitting identities does not multiply influence: each new identity needs its own bond and faces the same verification risk. The attacker must therefore lock up capital and risk losing it for every Sybil identity, making a cheap swarm costly. Even a market for nectar, shale, or oasis credits can use this rule.
